I will keep my land split between cotton and maize, but I will lean more on cotton because that is the crop system I know best and it usually matches my experience and labor rhythm. I am 50, I have farmed for 15 years, and some people in my family work off-farm, so I will not choose a plan that is too complicated or too risky. I have well irrigation, so I can support cotton through the key water periods, and I will use that advantage instead of depending only on rain. I will put the larger share of my 16.9 mu into cotton for cash income, and I will keep a smaller area in maize because it is steady and familiar. I will use better seed on both crops, not the lowest-input path, because I want more stable emergence and yield. I will use moderate fertilizer rates, not extreme ones, because I want to control costs while still feeding the crop properly. I will use rotary tillage because it is simpler and fits how I would manage the field at the start of the season. I will irrigate cotton more times than maize, and I will spray pesticides more on cotton because cotton usually needs closer pest control. My goal is steady production, manageable labor, and less chance of losing money in a bad year.
